chapter: Early bands and New Orleans musicians
title: Henry Fillmore pieces, brass bands, and Jack Teagarden as favorite
summary: He never played Fillmore pieces or brass bands, and names Jack Teagarden as his favorite trombonist, soon to play the Dream Room.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Do you remember any of these Henry Fillmore trombone pieces? Like, Lassus' trombone, Miss Trombone? No, I never played none of that stuff. Never played none of that stuff.
Never played any of it, no.
Did you ever play Josh's, uh, 76, uh, it was a march? No. Did you work in brass bands much?
No, no. Uh-uh. Mostly in six, seven piece bands.
Uh, I was wondering who your favorite trombone players were in those days?
Well, my favorite trombone player at that time was Jack Teagarden.
Jack, I thought Jack was about the best he was anyway.
He could still play, I heard him a couple months ago.
Yeah, he's still, he's still the best for me. What do you think? Fine.
I think he's gonna be down here before a while.

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: Yeah? He's gonna play at the Dream Room.
He's still top band for my mother. I'm gonna take you down there to see him.

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: I never was in a nightclub since I'm married, that's 40 years. But, uh, we're gonna go down there to see Jack at the Dream Room. Yeah.
